title: Agni, the head of heaven

words.context: Bhāskara: what the waters bring forth, the moving and unmoving (स्थावरजङ्गमाख्यानि)
Bhāskara: «जिन्वति वृष्ट्या तर्पयति», he quickens them with rain

sandhi.rule: -āḥ before a vowel loses its visarga

morphology.note: ककुद् ‘peak’; in the Saṃhitā it is written joined with patiḥ (ककुत्पतिः) though the two are separate words.

translation.literal: Agni is the head of heaven, its peak; this one is the lord of the earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
translation.readable: Agni is the summit of heaven and the lord of the earth; it is he who quickens the seed in the waters.

meaning: A gāyatrī verse that praises Agni as spanning the whole world: he is the head and summit of heaven, as the sun, and lord of the earth, as fire; and he quickens the ‘seeds of the waters’ — Bhāskara takes this as the rain by which Agni, in his middle form, nourishes all that moves and does not move. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (4.4.4.1) it belongs to the fire-altar (agnicayana) mantras; it is also Ṛgveda 8.44.16. Its use for Aṅgāraka, the red planet, belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the word aṅgāra itself means a glowing coal.
in_the_rite: The first mantra of Aṅgāraka’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, the graha’s own mantra; the two that follow (syonā pṛthivi, Mahānārāyaṇa 10.1.10, and kṣetrasya patinā) are named with it in the salutation.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «अयम् अग्निर् मूर्धा प्रधानभूतः दिवः द्युलोकस्य ककुत् उच्छ्रितः»; «अयमेव पृथिव्याः पतिः पाता; अग्निर् हि पृथिव्यात्मना वर्तते»; he quickens the seeds of the waters «माध्यमिकाग्निरूपेण», «वृष्ट्या तर्पयति».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa on RV 8.44.16 reads the summit of heaven as Agni in the form of the sun: «अयमग्निरादित्यरूपेण दिवो द्युलोकस्य ककुदुच्छ्रितो», and the quickening as the digestive fire within bodies: «जाठराग्निरूपेण जिन्वति प्रीणयति».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre gāyatrī. The Ṛgveda (8.44.16) has the same words.
